battle.name: 巴比倫對埃蘭的戰爭
battle.theater: 美索不達米亞中游巴比倫與蘇薩之間
battle.brief: 前十二世紀末，巴比倫城的卡西特王朝要結束蘇薩的埃蘭王國對美索不達米亞的半個世紀佔領，戰事沿幼發拉底河中游展開，爭的是穀物產區與被擄走的瑪爾杜克神像。卡面的埃及月牙劍屬同一世代的武備：它早被直刃短劍取代，只在神廟與墓葬中留作禮器，戰場上真正開鋒的仍是矛、弓與斧。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方是巴比倫與埃蘭，時間落在公元前十二世紀末至前十一世紀初，地點是美索不達米亞平原的東南角，核心在幼發拉底河中游的巴比倫尼尼微。巴比倫一方是卡西特王朝：自前1595年滅阿卡德帝國入主巴比倫城以來，這個王朝靠城邦的宗教與土地制度維持統治，歷數代君主之後，到這場戰爭時王位在 Itti-Marduk-balatu 及其後繼者 Marduk-shakit-ibni 手上。卡西特人原本是西南方的部族，統治結構是雙層的：外來王族掌軍權、佔有土地並主持祭祀，本地的神廟階層（尤其埃薩吉拉的瑪爾杜克神廟）握有穀物帳目、租佃與書吏，村社與商人則另立章程，軍隊以各城鎮抽丁的步兵為主，另有王室近衛。埃蘭一方是蘇薩的埃蘭王國：王室在伊朗西南的胡齊斯坦高原，宮廷與神廟（尤其拉馬什一系的神廟）靠本地農業、畜牧與銀礦支撐，軍隊以步兵與弓手為主，輔以車隊與數量不多的乘騎；攻城手段是斜坡、濠溝與撞槌。埃蘭自 Shutruk-Nahhunte 一世於前1155年攻入巴比倫尼尼微起，佔領美索不達米亞中部約半個世紀，所以這場衝突的實質，是巴比倫要把自己從埃蘭的宗主地位裡解救出來。埃及並非交戰方，但巴比倫在對抗埃蘭時曾向埃及求援，這一點正是本卡兵器會出現在這套戰役背景之中的原因。
countriesEn: The belligerents in this war were Babylon and Elam, the fighting falling in the late twelfth to the early eleventh century BC in the south-eastern corner of the Mesopotamian plain, with the centre of gravity in Babylonia on the middle Euphrates. On the Babylonian side stood the Kassite dynasty. Since the fall of the Akkadian empire in 1595 BC and the seizure of Babylon, this dynasty had held power by attaching itself to the religious and landed institutions of the city, and after several generations of kings it reached the period of this war with the throne in the hands of Itti-Marduk-balatu and his successor Marduk-shakit-ibni. The Kassites were originally a people from the south-west, and the structure of rule had two layers: an alien royal house holding the military command, owning land and officiating at sacrifice, and a local priestly class, above all the temple of Marduk at Esagila, controlling grain accounts, leases and the scribal corps, while village communities and merchants kept their own arrangements; the army was drawn mainly from foot soldiers levied in the towns, with a royal guard besides. On the Elamite side stood the kingdom of Elam with its capital at Susa. The royal house sat on the Khuzestan plateau in south-western Iran, and the court and its temples were sustained by local agriculture, herding and silver, the army being chiefly foot soldiers and archers, supported by chariots and a limited number of riders, with ramps, ditches and battering rams for siege work. Since Shutruk-Nahhunte I entered Babylonia in 1595 BC by the standard chronology, and with the sack of Sippar and the removal of the statue of Marduk to Susa around 1155 BC, Elam had occupied the middle of Mesopotamia for roughly half a century. The substance of the conflict, therefore, was Babylonian efforts to free itself from Elamite overlordship. Egypt was not a belligerent, but Babylon had turned to Egypt for help in its struggle against Elam, and that is the reason the weapon on this card belongs to the background of this series of wars.
people: 能點名的人不多，而且多半來自王表與殘存的年表。巴比倫一端，這場戰爭的關鍵君主通常被認為是 Itti-Marduk-balatu：他在位時埃蘭人仍據巴比倫城，他以「把埃蘭人逐出美索不達米亞」為號召，聯合神廟與商人的力量，最終在前1104年達到目的；其後繼者 Marduk-shakit-ibni 延續了這條政策，並與埃及保持書信往來。埃蘭一端，蘇薩的君主譜系在這段時間只剩輪廓：Shutruk-Nahhunte 一世即是前1155年掠奪西帕爾、把瑪爾杜克神像擄往蘇薩的那位；其子 Hazazu 亦有銘文存世；再往後的君主名與在位年只能大致排列，無法與每一年的戰事對上。有一位巴比倫王在更早一代卻留下清晰的名字——Marduk-zakir-shumi，他與埃蘭王、埃及王結成聯盟對抗亞述王 Tiglat-pileser I，最後在敗仗中被擒；這段聯盟被亞述的《同步史》記下，成為理解巴比倫、埃蘭、埃及三角關係的關鍵材料。人物群體方面：埃薩吉拉的祭司與財產管理員留下了大量土地與穀物的名目；那些堅持把神像迎回巴比倫的祭司集團，是推動反攻的主要力量；軍中則是各城鎮的徵召兵、埃蘭王室的常備步兵與車隊，以及可能隨商隊與傭兵契約進入軍中的努比亞與西奈戰士。埃及方面，與這場戰爭相關的名字屬於第二十一王朝的框架：三角洲的 Smendes、亞蒙神最高祭司 Herihor 與 Pinedjem 一系、率領「Ma 兵」的首領 Peftjauawybast，以及外籍近衛 Sherden。他們多半是盟友與旁觀者，但正是他們的配兵與結盟取向，讓月牙劍這一類兵器在近東戰爭裡留下了可追溯的位置。
peopleEn: Few names survive, and most of them come from king lists and fragmentary annals. On the Babylonian side the figure usually identified as the key ruler of this war is Itti-Marduk-balatu. While he reigned the Elamites still held Babylon, and he rallied the temples and the merchants around the slogan of driving the Elamites out of Mesopotamia, a goal reached in 1104 BC. His successor Marduk-shakit-ibni carried the same policy forward and kept up a correspondence with Egypt. On the Elamite side the royal succession of Susa survives only as an outline for this stretch: Shutruk-Nahhunte I is the king who sacked Sippar around 1155 BC and carried the statue of Marduk off to Susa; his son Hazazu is also attested by inscription, and the names and regnal years of the kings after him can only be ordered in a rough sequence, too roughly to be matched to individual years of fighting. One earlier Babylonian king, however, left a clear name: Marduk-zakir-shumi, who allied with a king of Elam and a king of Egypt against the Assyrian king Tiglat-pileser I and was taken prisoner after his defeat. That coalition is recorded in the Assyrian Synchronistic History and is the key document for understanding the triangle of Babylon, Elam and Egypt. As for groups of people: the priests and administrators of Esagila left behind a large number of land and grain entries; the priestly party that insisted on bringing the statue home was the chief driving force behind the counter-offensive; in the ranks were foot soldiers levied from the towns, the standing infantry and chariot crews of the Elamite royal house, and Nubian and Sinai warriors who may have entered service through caravan and mercenary contracts. On the Egyptian side the names associated with this war belong to the framework of the Twenty-First Dynasty: Smendes in the Delta, the High Priests Herihor and Pinedjem, the commander Peftjauawybast of the Ma troops, and the foreign guard of the Sherden. For the most part they were allies and witnesses, but it was their equipment and their alignment that left a traceable place for weapons such as the khopesh in the wars of the Near East.
kits: 卡面上的埃及月牙劍是外彎的單刃短刀，刃身由銅或青銅鑄成，沒有護手，砍下去不必拔起；這個形制在前十六世紀的埃及已是舊物。關鍵在於它被取代的時間：到了前1500年前後，埃及的野戰刀已由外彎的月牙形改為直刃無鐮的短劍，那種直刃刀更利、更耐折，也便於自鞘拔出；月牙劍從此退到兩個位置，一是神廟器物清冊、王室寶藏與貴族墓葬中的禮器，二是少量仍在使用的近身備用刀，軍人把它掛在腰帶上，近身格鬥時才拔。因此在前十一世紀的埃及軍中，說到「刀」指的是直刃短劍，月牙劍更多是象徵性的裝備。這個變化在整個東地中海是同步的：西奈與黎凡特的戰鬥遺物裡，直刃刀與鴨嘴斧逐漸並用，彎月形刀越來越少見。巴比倫與埃蘭的裝備體系與之相近而不同：矛以套筒固定的青銅矛頭安在木杆上，長槍列陣；弓是木胎角飾的複合弓，箭鏃為銅或青銅；斧為套筒青銅斧，砍伐與攻城兼用；盾有蒙皮圓盾，也有可立於身前的高盾；車為雙輪輕車，兩匹或四匹馬牽引，但這個年代車正逐步讓位給乘騎與馢運；攻城器械有斜坡、濠溝、土壘與撞槌。鐵在這時仍是稀罕物，主要出現在刀、匕首與飾件上，要到亞述統治美索不達米亞之後才會普及。埃及方面可對照的還有非對稱的埃及式弓、青銅箭鏃、圓盾、短柄斧、投石索，以及第二十一王朝仍在使用的輕車與「Ma 兵」裝備。
kitsEn: The Egyptian khopesh on the card is a curved single-edged short sword, its blade cast in copper or bronze, with no guard, so that it did not have to be wrenched free after a blow. By the sixteenth century BC this shape was already an antique in Egypt. What matters is the timing of its replacement: by about 1500 BC the fighting knife of Egypt had changed from the outward-curving crescent to a straight-edged, sickle-less short sword, which was sharper, tougher and easier to draw from a scabbard; the khopesh then retired into two positions, the temple inventory and the royal treasury as a ceremonial object, and the ranks of a small number of still-serviceable side knives that a soldier hung at his belt and drew only in close combat. So in the Egyptian army of the eleventh century BC, the word for a sword meant the straight-edged short sword, and the khopesh had become largely a symbol. The change ran synchronously across the whole eastern Mediterranean: in the combat debris of Sinai and the Levant the straight-edged sword and the duckbill axe came to be used together, and the crescent blade grew steadily rarer. The equipment system of Babylon and Elam was close to this and yet different: spears had copper or bronze socketed heads fixed to wooden shafts and were massed in ranks; the bow was a composite of wood with horn fittings, its arrowheads of copper or bronze; the axe was a socketed bronze axe used both for work and for assault; shields included round hide-covered types and tall shields that could be set on the ground in front of the man; the chariot was a light two-wheeled vehicle drawn by two or four horses, though at this date the chariot was giving way to riding and to pack animals; siege equipment comprised ramps, ditches, earthworks and battering rams. Iron was still a rarity, appearing mainly in blades, daggers and fittings, and did not become common until after the Assyrians took Mesopotamia. On the Egyptian side the comparable kit includes the asymmetric Egyptian bow, bronze arrowheads, round shields, short-hafted axes, the sling, and the light chariots and Ma troops' equipment still in use under the Twenty-First Dynasty.
tactics: 巴比倫與埃蘭的作戰方式都可以從更早的兩河流域傳統推想，但這場衝突有它自己的地理邏輯。巴比倫城坐落在幼發拉底河中游，河道既是屏障也是最短的補給線；埃蘭的遠征隊伍從蘇薩沿克爾克河與胡齊斯坦山麓南下，往往在春初河水泛濫、路可通行時出動，目標是巴比倫尼尼微周邊的穀物產區、蓄水池與廟產，奪走小麥、大麥、椰棗與牲畜，掠奪之外還要取得神像作為戰利品，這在兩河流域是公認的合法所得。防禦的一方因此採守城為本、出城殲敵為輔的辦法：先把渡口與灌溉渠上的橋樑控制住，用船隊巡弋幼發拉底，再在城外開闊地與來犯之師接戰；晚期巴比倫的步兵在這樣的戰役中習慣密集方陣前推，弓手在後或兩翼齊射，車隊用於突破缺口，盾牌遮蔽身前的箭。攻方埃蘭的戰術則是分隊掠奪與集中決戰的混合：輕裝縱隊快速推進，以弓手消耗守軍，待援兵與車隊集結後再作決定性衝擊，或者根本不打會戰，只把戰利品運回蘇薩——以兩河流域的糧食與交通條件看，後者常是更划算的選擇。補給端，埃蘭靠胡齊斯坦的銀與當地徵發，巴比倫靠尼普爾、希帕的穀物與河運，誰能先把船與糧食運到位，誰就決定戰役能拖多久。
tacticsEn: The ways of fighting of Babylon and Elam can both be reasoned from older Mesopotamian tradition, but this conflict has a geography of its own. Babylon sits on the middle Euphrates, and the river is at once a barrier and the shortest line of supply. The Elamite expeditionary columns came down from Susa along the Karun and the foothills of Khuzestan, and they habitually set out in early spring, when the rivers were in flood and the going was open, with the grain districts, the reservoirs and the temple estates around Babylonia as their object: they took wheat, barley, date palms and livestock, and beyond plain plunder they wanted the statues of the gods, which in Mesopotamia were recognised as legitimate spoil. The defence therefore worked city-first with a counterstroke in the open: control the fords and the bridges over the irrigation canals first, patrol the Euphrates with river craft, and then meet the invader in the open ground outside the walls. The late Babylonian infantry in such a war was accustomed to advance in dense formations, archers firing in volleys from the rear or the flanks, chariots used to open a gap, shields masking the body from arrows. The Elamite method mixed dispersed plunder with a concentrated decision: light columns pushing fast, archers wearing down the defenders, and a decisive charge once reinforcements and chariots had joined, or no battle at all, taking the loot back to Susa, which in a land where grain and transport were the binding constraint was often the cheaper choice. On the supply side, Elam drew on the silver of Khuzestan and on local requisition, while Babylon drew on the grain of Nippur and Sippar and on river transport; whoever got boats and food into place first decided how long the war could be drawn out.
data: 能核對的數字分三類。第一類是年表：中文的戰爭列表把此役繫於公元前1110年，學界一般只肯把相關事件放在前十二世紀末至前十一世紀初；巴比倫方面，卡西特王朝統治巴比倫尼尼微約自前1595年至前1155年，埃蘭的佔領約自前1155年至前1104年，而前1104年巴比倫人逐走埃蘭人、瑪爾杜克神像自蘇薩歸回，是這段故事最硬的一個座標。巴比倫王 Itti-Marduk-balatu 在位約前1129至前1108年，其後繼者 Marduk-shakit-ibni 在位約前1108至前1050年；再早一代的 Marduk-zakir-shumi 與埃蘭、埃及結盟對抗 Tiglat-pileser I（約前1114至前1076年在位），見於亞述的《同步史》，一般放在前1120年代。第二類是距離與地理：巴比倫城至蘇薩直線約三百七十公里，沿幼發拉底與胡齊斯坦山麓走約五百公里；巴比倫至西帕爾約六十公里，至尼普爾約一百六十公里，至烏爾約二百二十公里，埃蘭遠征隊伍實際要走的正是這條河谷路線；巴比倫對岸的渡口古籍稱普祖爾-馬爾杜克，扼住它就等於扼住東西往來。第三類是規模與物質：埃及的《薩利耶紙草書》與各代王家軍隊清冊可以見到弓手與僱傭兵的數目級別，亞述王室銘文則慣用「無數」「全境之兵」一類修辭，巴比倫與埃蘭的王室銘文同樣如此，因此雙方出動兵力只能說在數千至數萬的量級，沒有任何可靠文獻給出具體人數；冶金方面，銅與青銅仍是兵器主料，鐵在前十二至前十一世紀的美索不達米亞屬罕見材質，多見於刀、匕首與飾件，亞述人的大規模鐵器化要晚到前十至前九世紀。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is chronology: the Chinese list of battles ties this war to 1110 BC, while scholarship will only place the related events in the late twelfth to the early eleventh century BC. On the Babylonian side the Kassite dynasty held Babylonia from about 1595 to 1155 BC, the Elamite occupation ran from about 1155 to 1104 BC, and the year 1104, when the Babylonians drove out the Elamites and the statue of Marduk came back from Susa, is the hardest single fixed point in the story. Itti-Marduk-balatu reigned about 1129 to 1108 BC and his successor Marduk-shakit-ibni about 1108 to 1050 BC; the earlier Marduk-zakir-shumi and his alliance with Elam and Egypt against Tiglat-pileser I, who reigned about 1114 to 1076 BC, are recorded in the Assyrian Synchronistic History and are usually placed in the 1120s. The second class is distance and geography: about three hundred and seventy kilometres in a straight line from Babylon to Susa, roughly five hundred by the Euphrates and the foothills of Khuzestan; about sixty kilometres from Babylon to Sippar, about a hundred and sixty to Nippur, about two hundred and twenty to Ur, and the Elamite columns marched exactly this river route; the ford opposite Babylon, called Puzur-Marduk in the ancient texts, was the gate of all movement east and west. The third class is scale and material. The Papyrus Sallier I and the royal army lists of Egypt give orders of magnitude for archers and mercenaries, and Assyrian royal inscriptions habitually use formulas such as countless and the troops of the whole land, as do the Babylonian and Elamite royal texts; the forces on both sides can therefore only be said to lie in the range of thousands to tens of thousands, and no reliable document gives a figure. On metallurgy, copper and bronze were still the principal materials of arms, while iron in twelfth- to eleventh-century Mesopotamia was a rarity, appearing mostly in blades, daggers and fittings; the large-scale adoption of iron by the Assyrians belongs to the tenth and ninth centuries BC.
cause: 打起來的根由有四層。最遠的一層是結構性的：前1155年之後的美索不達米亞，實際統治者是外來的埃蘭人，巴比倫王室的權柄被壓到只剩神廟與稅收的餘緒，統治者與被統治者之間沒有共同的血緣與語言，這樣的佔領在政治上從來不穩。卡西特王族本身是由外來征服者建立的王朝，數代之後已與本地人口融為一體，卻仍被許多人視為不配坐王位的外人，驅逐埃蘭人於是同時成了民族訴求與階級訴求。第二層是物質的：巴比倫尼尼微的經濟建立在幼發拉底中游的灌溉農業上，小麥、大麥、椰棗與亞麻的產量集中在烏爾、尼普爾、希帕一線；埃蘭遠征的目標正是這些產區的穀物、牲畜與蓄水池，掠來的收成足以支撐蘇薩宮廷與神廟一整年的開支，這使襲掠變成一種制度化的年度行動，而不是偶發的破壞。第三層是宗教的：瑪爾杜克神像被帶到蘇薩，等於巴比倫的護符被擄走，王室的合法性與城邦的自我認同同時受損；對巴比倫人而言，奪回神像是國事，把神像迎回埃薩吉拉的穆薩拉被定為慶典，許多私人契約都把神像歸還列為條款。第四層是國際的：在北方，亞述正沿幼發拉底中游壓迫巴比倫，巴比倫若要同時對抗埃蘭與亞述，最自然的做法是向埃及求援，這正是《同步史》記載的巴比倫、埃蘭、埃及三方聯盟的政治背景。直接導火線沒有留下記載；較合理的推測是某一年春季埃蘭的掠奪隊伍深入巴比倫腹地，奪走大批穀物並擄走神像與工匠，巴比倫王於是點集城邦民兵與王室軍隊，順河谷南下反擊，戰事就在巴比倫城與蘇薩之間的走廊上展開。
causeEn: The reasons for the fighting have four layers. The most distant is structural: after 1155 BC the effective rulers of Mesopotamia were foreign Elamites, the authority of the Babylonian court had been reduced to what remained of the temples and the tax system, and ruler and ruled shared neither blood nor language, so that an occupation of this kind was never politically secure. The Kassite royal house had itself been founded by a conquering people; after several generations it had merged with the local population, yet it was still widely treated as an alien house not entitled to the throne, and driving out the Elamites was therefore at once a national demand and a class interest. The second layer is material. The economy of Babylonia rested on irrigated farming along the middle Euphrates, and the yield of wheat, barley, dates and flax lay in the strip of Ur, Nippur and Sippar. The Elamite expeditions came precisely for the grain, the livestock and the reservoirs of those districts, and what they took was enough to support the court and the temples of Susa for a whole year, which turned raid into a regular institutional campaign rather than an occasional raid. The third layer is religious: with the statue of Marduk carried off to Susa, the talisman of Babylon was in captivity, and the legitimacy of the monarchy and the identity of the city were wounded in the same stroke. For the Babylonians the recovery of the statue was a matter of state; its return to Esagila was appointed as a festival, and many private contracts made the restoration of the statue a clause. The fourth layer is international: to the north Assyria was bearing down on Babylon along the middle Euphrates, and if Babylon was to stand against Elam and Assyria at once, the obvious course was to seek Egyptian support, which is the political background to the Babylonian, Elamite and Egyptian coalition recorded in the Synchronistic History. No record of the immediate occasion survives. The likeliest reconstruction is that in some spring an Elamite plunder column pushed deep into the Babylonian interior, carrying off grain and taking gods and craftsmen, and that the king then called out the militia of the city-states together with the royal troops and counter-attacked down the river valley, so that the war was fought along the corridor between Babylon and Susa.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果，是巴比倫尼尼微在埃蘭佔領半個世紀之後，於前1104年前後重新回到巴比倫人自己手裡：埃蘭人撤出巴比倫城與其附屬城邑，瑪爾杜克神像自蘇薩迎回埃薩吉拉，掠走的穀物與牲畜雖多數已被消耗，仍有相當部分追回或以贖金抵償；卡西特王朝得以在巴比倫延續下去，王位傳到 Marduk-shakit-ibni 及其後繼者，這段時間差說明驅逐埃蘭不是一次反攻的成果，而是長達半個世紀的反覆拉鋸。長期看，這場衝突是巴比倫與埃蘭三百年爭奪的收尾：此前巴比倫一系先後臣服於海彼斯人、蘇美爾諸王朝與阿卡德，之後又被卡西特人取代，每一代強權都把這裡當作戰利品與資源地；巴比倫尼尼微在這三百年裡唯一穩定累積的，是它的神廟經濟、城牆與泥板檔案，這些東西讓它在每次易主之後都能重新站起來，卻始終沒有讓它成為一個真正的帝國。也正因如此，前1047年塞沙爾特進軍巴比倫尼尼微時，城市幾乎沒有像後來亞述人那樣的抵抗，一個半世紀之後的亞述統治才是它真正的終局。軍備層面的後果更為長遠：這場戰爭之後數十年裡，銅器仍撐起兩河流域全部的兵員，而鐵先出現在刀與飾件上；與此同時，整個東地中海的近身兵器由月牙形的彎刀轉向直刃短劍與鴨嘴斧的組合，這個轉變在埃及的軍械清冊與西奈、黎凡特的戰鬥遺物裡都可辨認；埃及的月牙劍並未消亡，它退居神廟器物與王室寶藏，成為一件象徵物而非一件武器。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the war was that Babylonia, after half a century of Elamite occupation, returned to Babylonian hands around 1104 BC: the Elamites withdrew from the city of Babylon and its dependent towns, the statue of Marduk was brought back from Susa to Esagila, and of the grain and livestock that had been carried off, much was already consumed, but a considerable part was recovered or compensated in ransom. The Kassite dynasty was able to continue at Babylon, the throne passing to Marduk-shakit-ibni and his successors, and that stretch of time shows that the expulsion of Elam was not the result of a single counter-offensive but of a half-century of repeated pulling and hauling. In the long run the war closes three centuries of contention between Babylon and Elam. Before it, one Babylonian line had submitted in turn to the Amorites, the Sumerian dynasties and Akkad, and was then replaced by the Kassites; every generation of power treated the city as spoil and as a resource. The only thing Babylonia accumulated steadily across those three centuries was its temple economy, its walls and its clay tablets, and those allowed it to stand up again after each change of masters, but they never made it an empire in its own right. For that very reason, when the Chaldean king marched into Babylon in 1047 BC, the city offered almost none of the resistance that the Assyrians would later have to break, and the real end for it came a century and a half later under Assyrian rule. The consequences at the level of armament reach further. For decades after this war copper still carried the whole military establishment of Mesopotamia while iron first appeared in blades and fittings; at the same time the close-combat weapon across the whole eastern Mediterranean shifted from the curved crescent blade to the pairing of the straight-edged short sword with the duckbill axe, a change that can be read in the Egyptian armorial lists and in the combat debris of Sinai and the Levant. The Egyptian khopesh did not disappear: it retired to the temple inventories and the royal treasury, and became a symbol rather than a weapon.
result: 勝負與細節都難以還原，必須先把話說在前面。巴比倫方面的年表有長段缺頁，埃蘭的記錄則散佚在蘇薩的殘簡與後世的引用裡，這一場戰爭沒有留下任何一份雙方的戰報；具體的戰鬥序列、雙方出兵的數目、是否真的在開闊地交過手，都只能從結局去反推。可確定的是最終的結局：埃蘭人放棄對巴比倫尼尼微的佔領，退出美索不達米亞中部，前1104年之後巴比倫城再度由巴比倫人自己的君王掌控，瑪爾杜克神像歸位，戰俘與被擄人口陸續返鄉。就過程而言，最可能的輪廓是：埃蘭一方以分隊掠奪為主，試圖在巴比倫的防禦薄弱處奪取穀物與神像；巴比倫一方以守城與反擊相配合，用河運與游擊拖住埃蘭的縱隊，同時在埃蘭遠征隊伍回程時截擊，最終以一次次的小勝累積成埃蘭的退場。這種不求一戰定勝負、以消耗換退場的格局，也正是巴比倫在亞述壓力下最終能撐住的同一套辦法。戰爭對武器制度的影響則可清楚看出：銅與青銅仍是兩河流域的主料，鐵仍罕見；月牙劍所代表的彎刀傳統，在埃及與黎凡特退居禮器，在美索不達米亞則早已讓位給直刃短劍與斧；車隊的戰役角色下降、乘騎與馢運上升，騎兵的前奏在這一時期已經聽得見。
resultEn: Neither the outcome nor the detail can be reconstructed, and that has to be said at the start. The Babylonian annals have long missing stretches and the Elamite record survives only in fragments from Susa and in later quotation, and no battle report survives from either side. The order of the fighting, the numbers on each side and whether the two armies ever met in the open can only be reasoned backwards from the end. What is certain is the end itself: the Elamites gave up their occupation of Babylonia, withdrew from the middle of Mesopotamia, and after 1104 BC the city of Babylon was once again governed by its own king, the statue of Marduk was restored, and prisoners and deported people returned over the following years. As for the process, the likeliest outline is this: on the Elamite side, dispersed plunder was the method, an attempt to seize grain and gods wherever Babylonian defence was thin; on the Babylonian side, city defence and counterstroke were combined, using river transport and raiding parties to hold up the Elamite columns and striking them on their return march, so that a series of small successes added up to the Elamite withdrawal. That pattern, trading decisive battle for attrition in the hope of driving the enemy off, is the same device by which Babylon was later able to hold out under Assyrian pressure. The effect of the war on the armoury of the age is clearer: copper and bronze remained the principal materials of Mesopotamia, iron remained rare; the tradition of the curved blade that the khopesh represents retired to ceremonial use in Egypt and the Levant and had long been displaced by the straight-edged short sword and the axe in Mesopotamia; and the declining war role of the chariot, together with the rise of riding and of pack animals, means that the cavalry of the next age could already be heard approaching.
